messages.author: d43fdd1225307dbb
messages.subject: Testing for multiple factors
parts:
Hi,

I have a rather complex experimental design (WGBS data), and would like to test multiple factors at the same time as well as testing by contrast using the regression analysis implemented in methylKit. At the moment calculateDiffmeth(), only allows to test for a single treatment (i.e. factor of two levels). Ideally, one would simply provide a model matrix and contrast matrix to the function (as for example in the limma package).

Is that possible?

Thanks a lot.
Angelika

messages.author: ab8277113f65c05e
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] Testing for multiple factors
parts:
It is not possible although you can get pretty close to what you want by altering the treatment vector for comparisons of interest and covariates argument to control other covariates and running calculateDiffMeth multiple times 

Best
Altuna

messages.author: ab8277113f65c05e
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] Testing for multiple factors
parts:
It allows for more levels but you can’t apply contrasts as in limma. As I wrote comparisons you would get from simple contrasts and probably some complicated ones can be achieved using reorganize() and/or resetting the treatment vector for comparison of interest. 

Best
Altuna
